description: We are team Apollo 3! We are building an interactive Python dashboard for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. Our goal is to make it easy to analyze, compare, and visualize Mars.
summary: The Mars Navigation System is an advanced autonomous mission control and pathfinding web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Designed to overcome the lack of Martian GPS networks and severe Earth-to-Mars communication delays, the system integrates high-resolution USGS Mars MOLA GeoTIFF elevation data to perform precise geospatial analysis and slope gradient evaluations.   The platform features a sophisticated dual-route A* pathfinding engine that computes and compares Route A (Safest) and Route B (Shortest), intelligently bypassing severe terrain hazards, active dust storms, and dangerous radiation anomalies. Operators benefit from an interactive React-Leaflet tactical map, real-time EVA astronaut biometrics, critical environmental telemetry, and adaptive payload recommendations. For inclusive global and local accessibility, the interface incorporates instant, zero-reload bilingual localization supporting both English and Myanmar languages seamlessly. Engineered for robust operational performance, the full-stack architecture decouples a Next.js TypeScript frontend hosted on Vercel from a high-performance Python FastAPI geospatial backend deployed on Render. Continuous 24/7 reliability is maintained through automated UptimeRobot HTTP keep-alive pings, eliminating cold starts and ensuring uninterrupted readiness for live mission demonstrations and international space exploration judging.
details: The Mars Navigation System is an advanced autonomous mission control and pathfinding web application engineered specifically for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Designed to tackle the critical challenges of planetary exploration—such as the total absence of a Martian GPS satellite network and severe Earth-to-Mars communication delays ranging from 4 to 24 minutes—the platform empowers rovers and astronauts with intelligent geospatial navigation and real-time safety guardrails. At its core, the system ingests high-resolution 25MB USGS Mars MOLA Digital Elevation Model (DEM) GeoTIFF raster data into a high-performance Python FastAPI backend. Utilizing rasterio, numpy, and a robust cost-weighted A* pathfinding algorithm, the geospatial engine computes and evaluates two distinct trajectories: Route A (Safest), which heavily penalizes steep slopes exceeding 22 degrees, active dust storms, and thermal radiation zones to prioritize vehicle stability, and Route B (Shortest), which optimizes for minimum travel distance while transparently exposing risk spikes in rock counts and energy consumption. Operators interact through a modern Next.js TypeScript frontend deployed on Vercel, featuring an interactive React-Leaflet tactical map. The comprehensive mission control HUD provides real-time multi-hazard overlays—including terrain hazards, dust storms, and dedicated purple dashed radiation circles—alongside live EVA astronaut biometrics, surface temperature telemetry, wind speeds, and continuous DEM elevation profiles. Furthermore, the platform integrates smart safety mechanisms like Auto-Snap terrain validation, adaptive required payload kits, and timestamped system logs.To ensure inclusive global and regional accessibility, the application incorporates an instant, zero-reload bilingual localization engine built with React Context, allowing seamless switching between English and native Myanmar terminology. Maintained 24/7 with zero cold starts through automated UptimeRobot keep-alive pings to the Render cloud backend, the Mars Navigation System delivers a robust, production-ready solution for planetary exploration.
